name: Indigo dyeing on the north coast of Peru
summary: Cotton cloth at Huaca Prieta on Peru's north coast was dyed blue with indigo about 6,000 years ago, the earliest chemically identified use of indigo anywhere.
description: At Huaca Prieta, indigoid dye coloured cotton warp yarns used to make striped, weft-twined fabric. Chromatography detected indigoid components in five of eight sampled textiles, including specimen 2009.052.01.B&C from stratum 44. The dye plant and preparation method remain uncertain.

impact.note: Indigo-dyed cloth is shown at this one site over several thousand years, and descent of the wider Andean dyeing tradition from it is plausible but not shown, so reach stays regional; blue on cloth improved an existing textile craft, and a few later dye combinations built on it.

date.label: about 6200 to 6000 years ago
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Two weft-twined, blue-striped textiles were recovered from stratum 44. Chromatography on specimen 2009.052.01.B&C identified indigotin and indirubin in its blue yarn.

evidence.supports: The textile was made with plied warp yarns, including blue cotton stripes. Chromatography identified indigoid compounds on a yarn sample.
The dated contexts above and below stratum 44 provide a stratigraphic age estimate for the early indigo specimen.

evidence.locator: Fig. 12.1d and Color, Pigment, and Dye
evidence.supports: Illustrates the same inspected indigo specimen and identifies its excavation stratum.

events.scope: Production of indigo-striped cotton fabric, evidenced by the stratum 44 textile assemblage.
events.caveats: The age comes from stratum 44’s position between dated levels. The publications assign different phase labels to the specimen and agree on its stratum and identity.

date.label: c. 6,000 years ago
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: Blue colour on 6000-year-old cotton fabrics from Huaca Prieta on the north coast of Peru was analysed and positively identified as an indigoid dye (indigotin); 6000 years before 1950 is about 4050 BCE.

evidence.supports: 6000-year-old cotton fabrics from the Preceramic site of Huaca Prieta on the north coast of Peru retained traces of a blue pigment that was analyzed and positively identified as an indigoid dye (indigotin)

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: The textiles are dated by their position between radiocarbon-dated strata, not directly.
Which plant supplied the dye, and whether it was prepared in a fermentation vat, are not established; the paper names Indigofera as most likely and treats vat dyeing as a hypothesis.

Whether later Andean and Mesoamerican indigo dyeing descends from this north-coast tradition is not shown; the next identified blue dyes in the Americas are from Ocucaje and Paracas, around 2500-2250 cal BP.
The Huaca Prieta coordinates were entered from memory (the mound lies in the El Brujo complex near the mouth of the Chicama river) and should be checked against a gazetteer.

unresolved.about: Sequence of fibre preparation and colouring
unresolved.note: The striped fabric incorporates plied cotton yarn with indigo. The archaeological study does not identify the dyeing stage relative to spinning or the source of the yarn in this specimen.

research.note: The paper states that the Huaca Prieta fabrics are the earliest known use of indigo in the world, about 1,500 years before the earliest reported Old World use in Fifth Dynasty Egypt; it counts chemically confirmed examples only.

links.statement: Did the plied cotton used in the indigo-striped cloth come from the same yarn-making tradition as the earlier cotton yarn at Huaca Prieta?
links.scope: Two separate finds from the HP-3 trench. The earlier find is yarn AA82121 from stratum 52. The later find is the indigo-striped specimen 2009.052.01.B&C from stratum 44.
links.caveats: Spinning location, fibre source and the order of spinning and dyeing remain open.

evidence.supports: Documents plied yarns in the warps and identifies an indigoid dye in the blue yarn sampled from the cloth.
Radiocarbon analysis independently dates an earlier cotton yarn from the same site and trench.
Documents varieties of yarn in the broader textile assemblage and illustrates the identified indigo specimen.

links.finding: The indigo-striped cloth incorporates plied cotton yarn. The dated yarn and the broader textile catalogue do not identify the cloth’s yarn supplier or establish continuity of production between these contexts.
